notes: v10.4 BUILD REFRESH (2026-11-20, b4762 — the nineteenth cut — nothing is written where nothing was said; spelled letters stay as spelled; a word is not an acronym, notarized): (1) Nothing is added where nothing was said. When the key was held after the speaker had stopped, a recovery step that listens a second time could write words over the quiet ("…and I want you" came out with five invented words after it). Every word that step wants to add must now have a timestamp and real sound under it; a word without them is refused. A doubted ending over a silent tail that no second listen can hear is refused as well. (2) Letters you spell stay as you spelled them. "Nikki, N-I-K-I" lost its spelled letters because they were read as a garbled repeat of the word before. A form spelled letter by letter is never collapsed into its neighbour. (3) A word in capitals is not an acronym. "Shot 1" was written "SHOT1" because any capital-letter token before a number was glued to it. A common English word
